skill.name: specdd-cli
skill.description: Use the specdd CLI to discover SpecDD context, inspect specs, lint .sdd files, and run requested setup or updates.
skill.summary: Use SpecDD CLI commands to resolve project specs before implementation.
skill.author: specdd

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, documented CLI examples, and local path descriptions. The skill guides explicit local specdd CLI use, requires operator intent for setup or updates, and forbids automatic installation. No prompt injection, credential access, network exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: SpecDD projects need targeted context before agents read or change files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use the specdd CLI for focused discovery, inspection, and linting.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether the specdd CLI is available before use.
Uses resolve to find SpecDD context for a target path.
Uses inspect to list specs and selected sections for a path.
Uses lint to validate edited .sdd files.
Guides init and update only when the operator explicitly asks.
limitations: Requires an existing SpecDD project with .specdd/bootstrap.md unless adoption is requested.
Does not install the specdd CLI automatically.
Does not grant write authority from resolve output alone.
Depends on the local specdd CLI behavior and project files.

use_cases.title: Prepare an implementation task
use_cases.description: Resolve the governing specs for a target file before editing code.

use_cases.title: Author or update specs
use_cases.description: Inspect nearby SpecDD files to choose the right boundary for a new or changed spec.

use_cases.title: Validate contract changes
use_cases.description: Lint edited .sdd files and summarize remaining diagnostics before completion.

prompt_templates.title: Find Spec Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single target path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SpecDD CLI to resolve context for [target path]. Summarize governing specs before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Subtree
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for mapping available specs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [path] with focused sections. Report which specs exist and which sections matter for this task.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Edited Specs
prompt_templates.prompt: Lint the edited SpecDD files. Explain whether validation passed and list any diagnostics that still need work.

prompt_templates.title: Update Framework Carefully
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for explicit framework maintenance.
prompt_templates.prompt: When I explicitly ask, update this project with the SpecDD CLI. Report changed bootstrap files and reread affected context.

output_examples.input: Resolve context for a component before editing it.
output_examples.output: A concise report listing relevant specs, reviewed sections, and any authority gaps before code changes.

output_examples.input: Inspect a directory that may need a new spec.
output_examples.output: A mapped summary of nearby specs, their selected sections, and the likely placement boundary.
A validation summary that states whether lint passed, names files with diagnostics, and identifies remaining fixes.

best_practices: Run CLI commands from the project root when possible.
Use section filters to keep output focused.
Lint edited specs before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when the project lacks .specdd/bootstrap.md.
Do not auto-install specdd when the CLI is missing.
Do not treat resolve output as permission to edit files.

faq.question: Does this skill install specdd?
faq.answer: No. It checks for the CLI and reports when it is unavailable.

faq.question: When should I use resolve?
faq.answer: Use resolve when a task has a concrete target path and needs relevant SpecDD context.

faq.question: When should I use inspect?
faq.answer: Use inspect to map existing specs or review selected sections for a path.

faq.question: When should I run lint?
faq.answer: Run lint after creating or editing .sdd files, starting with the narrowest changed path.

faq.question: Can resolve output authorize edits?
faq.answer: No. Resolve helps find context, but direct spec text still governs write authority.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
